result.label: Own-price elasticity, 330ml can
result.rationale: Smallest, most impulse-driven format; set near the elastic end of the brief's -0.8 to -2.5 CPG range.
result.reference: Context only, not a fitted value. A 2024 meta-analysis of U.S. food demand elasticities (Jeon, Hoang, Thompson and Abler) finds household scanner data tends to give more elastic own-price estimates (https://pure.psu.edu/en/publications/a-meta-analysis-of-us-food-demand-elasticities-to-detect-the-impa/). It does not cover soft drinks specifically, so the values here are illustrative. A Marketing Science Institute working paper (Bray, Sanders and Stamatopoulos) finds observational scanner price variation does not reproduce experimental elasticities (https://www.msi.org/working-paper/observational-price-variation-in-scanner-data-cannot-reproduce-experimental-price-elasticities/), so the value carries a range that drives the sensitivity bands.

result.label: Promo depth saturation rate
result.rationale: Shapes f(depth)=1-exp(-k*depth); k=6 gives strong saturation by 30% depth.
result.reference: Modelling choice. A vendor page (Tellius, marketing material, not research) describes the same concepts the engine mirrors: lift against a baseline, pull-forward and cannibalisation (https://www.tellius.com/cpg/trade-promotion-analytics). The values here are illustrative.

result.label: Gabor-Granger acceptance threshold
result.rationale: Highest tested price still accepted by at least this share of respondents is offered as a candidate.

result.label: Gabor-Granger default price grid (x reference price)
result.rationale: Default tested prices as multiples of the pack's reference price, spanning the engine's observed price range and a little beyond so edge refusals stay visible.
result.reference: Synthetic consumer-evidence input supplied by the analyst; nothing is estimated from real respondents.

result.label: Van Westendorp price grid step (INR)
result.rationale: Resolution of the price grid on which cumulative curves are intersected; coarser grids move intersections by at most one step.
result.reference: Synthetic consumer-evidence input supplied by the analyst; nothing is estimated from real respondents.

result.label: Conjoint respondent heterogeneity weight
result.rationale: Scales a respondent's price and promotion part-worths by 1 + weight x (sensitivity - 0.5), where 0.5 is the midpoint of the 0-1 sensitivity scale. Deterministic; nothing is fitted.
result.reference: Synthetic consumer-evidence input supplied by the analyst; nothing is estimated from real respondents.

result.label: Supplied synthetic conjoint part-worths
result.rationale: Illustrative part-worths supplied by the analyst. They are inputs to a deterministic multinomial-logit simulation and are never estimated or fitted from data. price_slope is utility per +100% price versus the pack's reference price.
result.reference: Synthetic consumer-evidence input supplied by the analyst; nothing is estimated from real respondents.

result.note: Modeled by the deterministic engine; gp changes are per week for the focal brand against the baseline.

caveats: All modeled outcomes depend on the assumption sets listed for each scenario, including price–elasticity and promo‑response assumptions (e.g., 1.assumption_ids, 2.assumption_ids, 4.assumption_ids, 5.assumption_ids).

Comparisons here focus on the Aurora 1.5L pack’s own gross profit; portfolio_gp is reported but was not used to choose the best mechanic for this specific pack. The portfolio effects in 2.portfolio_gp.value and 4.portfolio_gp.value differ slightly from 1.portfolio_gp.value and should be considered separately if total‑portfolio profit is also an objective.

claims.label: Modeled
claims.text: In the cost‑neutral baseline with no promotion, Aurora 1.5L has modeled weekly gross profit of 30,897.71700847693 INR (1.gp.Aurora-bottle_1500ml.value, evaluation_tool_call_id=call_0005).

claims.label: Modeled
claims.text: Under a 20% TPR on Aurora 1.5L for 1 week per month, modeled weekly gross profit for Aurora 1.5L is 29,133.73232603424 INR (2.gp.Aurora-bottle_1500ml.value, evaluation_tool_call_id=call_0005), with the difference versus baseline explained by higher promo funding of 13,959.99 INR, trade support of −6,603.46 INR, and cogs impact of −9,120.52 INR (2.focal_bridge.promo, 2.focal_bridge.trade, 2.focal_bridge.cogs).

claims.label: Modeled
claims.text: Under a 15% feature & display on Aurora 1.5L for 1 week per month, modeled weekly gross profit for Aurora 1.5L is 30,847.840648294936 INR (4.gp.Aurora-bottle_1500ml.value, evaluation_tool_call_id=call_0005), with the gap to baseline driven by promo funding of 14,877.32 INR, partially offset by trade of −5,207.36 INR and cogs of −9,719.84 INR (4.focal_bridge.promo, 4.focal_bridge.trade, 4.focal_bridge.cogs).

claims.label: Modeled
claims.text: In the downside input‑cost stress without promo, Aurora 1.5L has modeled weekly gross profit of 28,120.406603536452 INR (5.gp.Aurora-bottle_1500ml.value, evaluation_tool_call_id=call_0005), fully explained by higher cost of goods of −11,042.48 INR versus the cost‑neutral baseline (5.focal_bridge.cogs).

recommendations: R1 (based on M1, M3, M4): Prioritize Aurora 1.5L at regular shelf price with no promotion as the primary mechanic when the goal is to maximize modeled weekly gross profit after pull‑forward, since it delivers the highest gross profit for the pack among all supported scenarios (M1, M3, M4).

R2 (based on M3): If a promotion is required for strategic or retailer reasons, use a 15% feature & display for 1 week per month on Aurora 1.5L rather than a 20% TPR, as it preserves gross profit closer to the no‑promo baseline while still providing some promotional support (M3).

R3 (based on M2): Avoid a 20% TPR for 1 week per month as the default promo for Aurora 1.5L when profit is the key objective, because its higher promo and trade funding reduce modeled gross profit for the pack more than the uplift in volume compensates (M2).
refusals: The scenario “High-lift but risky: 30% BOGO-style promo on Aurora 1.5L, 1 week per month” was refused because: “Aurora-bottle_1500ml: requested price/promo combination has no local observations (count=0)” and therefore has no supported profit estimate.
answer.summary:
For Aurora 1.5L, the highest modeled gross profit after pull‑forward among supported promotion scenarios is with no promotion at regular price.

Across the tested mechanics and depths:
- Baseline (no promo) gross profit for Aurora 1.5L is 30,897.71700847693 INR per week (1.gp.Aurora-bottle_1500ml.value, evaluation_tool_call_id=call_0005).
- A 20% TPR for 1 week per month lowers gross profit for Aurora 1.5L to 29,133.73232603424 INR (2.gp.Aurora-bottle_1500ml.value, evaluation_tool_call_id=call_0005), driven by higher promo funding and trade costs more than offsetting the volume benefit (2.focal_bridge.promo, 2.focal_bridge.trade, 2.focal_bridge.cogs).
- A 15% feature & display for 1 week per month yields gross profit for Aurora 1.5L of 30,847.840648294936 INR (4.gp.Aurora-bottle_1500ml.value, evaluation_tool_call_id=call_0005), slightly below the no‑promo baseline and shaped by increased promo funding largely netted off by cogs and trade effects (4.focal_bridge.promo, 4.focal_bridge.trade, 4.focal_bridge.cogs).
- The 30% BOGO‑style promo scenario was refused by the model and provides no valid profit estimate.

Given these modeled outcomes, the best profit after pull‑forward for Aurora 1.5L, among supported cases, comes from running the pack at regular price with no promotion, with 15% feature & display the least dilutive promo option tested.

A downside input‑cost stress without promo reduces Aurora 1.5L gross profit to 28,120.406603536452 INR (5.gp.Aurora-bottle_1500ml.value, evaluation_tool_call_id=call_0005), with the change versus the cost‑neutral baseline fully driven by higher cost of goods (5.focal_bridge.cogs).
